item.title: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
item.dc:creator: Huanhuan Cao
Yanghui Chen
Xiaoyi Liu
Chenwei Lin
Qi Zhang
Jun Yang
Ke Li
Shusi Ding
item.description:
Authors: Huanhuan Cao, Yanghui Chen, Xiaoyi Liu, Chenwei Lin, Qi Zhang, Jun Yang, Ke Li, Shusi Ding, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Aortic aneurysm and dissection (AAD) are life-threatening cardiovascular diseases with limited therapeutic options. It is essential to identify new risk factors and therapeutic targets for AAD. Recent evidence has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in AAD, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a gut microbiota–derived metabolite, is associated with increased risk for AAD. Our study illustrates that elevated plasma PAGln levels were independently associated with increased AAD risk in a clinical cohort comprising 1,144 individuals. Exogenous PAGln supplementation exacerbated AAD in male mice, whereas AAV8-mediated hepatic knockdown of Glyat reduced circulating metabolite levels and ameliorated AAD. We further demonstrated that the elevated PAGln levels observed in disease are gut microbiota–dependent in origin. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that PAGln exacerbates AAD by expanding a pro-inflammatory IL6 (high) macrophage subpopulation. Mechanistically, PAGln directly binds to integrin α5β1 and downregulates the repressive H3K27me3 levels via the integrin α5β1–integrin-linked kinase (ILK)–lysine demethylase 6B (KDM6B) signaling, thereby enhancing IL6 transcriptional permissiveness. Genetic ablation of integrin β1, the receptor for PAGln, effectively ameliorated AAD in male mice. Our findings identify PAGln is associated with increased risk for AAD and reveal its potential as a therapeutic target.

item.title: Rethinking Klebsiella pneumoniae vaccines: from protective immunity to rational vaccine design
item.dc:creator: Sonia Nicchi
Suncong Zhou
Mariagrazia Pizza
item.description:
Authors: Sonia Nicchi, Suncong Zhou, Mariagrazia Pizza
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11960
Abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae infections cause hundreds of thousands of deaths annually, yet a licensed vaccine remains elusive. Current strategies targeting capsular polysaccharides and lipopolysaccharides show promise but face limitations due to the complexity of Klebsiella pathogenesis and incomplete understanding of protective immunity. This Review highlights the critical barriers hindering broad protection against K. pneumoniae . We argue that next-generation vaccines require a paradigm shift, integrating antigen discovery, systems immunology and translational models to define conserved protective targets and immune correlates. This holistic strategy is essential to predict vaccine efficacy and finally combat this escalating global health threat.

item.title: Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
item.dc:creator: Ka-Yiu Edwin Kong
Cécile Debarnot
Christian Ochs
Matti Myllykoski
Denís Arribas Blanco
Christian Renz
Susmitha Shankar
Vivien A. C. Schoonenberg
item.description:
Authors: Ka-Yiu Edwin Kong, Cécile Debarnot, Christian Ochs, Matti Myllykoski, Denís Arribas Blanco, Christian Renz, Susmitha Shankar, Vivien A. C. Schoonenberg, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11962
Abstract: Abstract The GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase is a multisubunit E3 conserved across eukaryotes. GID/CTLH has been implicated in a variety of processes, including metabolic regulation, cell proliferation, embryonic development and cell differentiation. However, our understanding of substrate recognition by GID/CTLH remains incomplete. Here, we characterize the regulation, specificity and functions of the putative substrate receptor Gid11 in budding yeast. We find that upon its expression during the switch of carbon source from glucose to ethanol, Gid11 associates with the core GID complex, likely assembling into a ring-like complex. Through systematic mutagenesis, we identify a negatively charged pocket on Gid11 that binds substrates carrying N-terminal degrons starting with threonine and define the Thr/N-degron motif. Such Thr/N-degrons are exposed upon co-translational removal of the initiator methionine, while escaping N-terminal acetylation. Finally, we show that during the glucose-to-ethanol transition, GID Gid11 targets for degradation factors linked to ribosomal biogenesis, amino acid, nucleotide and central carbon metabolism, opposing the established role of GID during the reverse transition from ethanol to glucose. Taken together, our results establish Gid11 as a bona fide GID substrate receptor and highlight GID as a regulator of metabolic transitions.

item.title: Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
item.dc:creator: Timothy F. Campbell
Jesse Garcia Castillo
Sebastian Fernandez
Ola Mostafa
Diego Gonzalez Ventura
Jenna Vickery
Stefan Homentcovschi
Nicole Flores Hernandez
item.description:
Authors: Timothy F. Campbell, Jesse Garcia Castillo, Sebastian Fernandez, Ola Mostafa, Diego Gonzalez Ventura, Jenna Vickery, Stefan Homentcovschi, Nicole Flores Hernandez, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Toll-like receptors (TLRs) support T cell priming in lymphatic tissues, but whether TLR stimulation within tumors also affects T cell function locally remains undefined. Here, we show that TLR2 signaling is necessary to promote CD8 + T cell-mediated tumor control by dual intravenous and intratumoral delivery of attenuated Listeria monocytogenes (IV + IT Lm ). TLR2 signaling supports T cell priming in the spleen during IV infection, but unexpectedly, TLR2 is also critical for the activity of anti- Lm CD8 + T cells in tumors upon IT Lm injection. TLR2 signaling is unique among all TLRs in its capacity to drive a cDC2-dependent reduction in regulatory T cells (Treg) and destabilize Foxp3 expression. TLR2-mediated Treg destabilization correlates with increased tumor antigen cross-presentation and stronger antitumor CD8 + T cell responses. Ultimately, TLR2-dependent Treg depletion is required for tumor control by IV + IT Lm . These findings reveal a novel role for TLR2 activation by bacteria in tumors to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance tumor-specific T cell responses.

item.title: 3D-MINSTED nanoscopy and protein tracking in densely labelled living cells
item.dc:creator: Julius Bernhard Peters
Christopher Heidebrecht
Michael Weber
Marcel Leutenegger
Stefan W. Hell
item.description:
Authors: Julius Bernhard Peters, Christopher Heidebrecht, Michael Weber, Marcel Leutenegger, Stefan W. Hell
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11965
Abstract: Abstract Investigating the movements and conformational changes of proteins in living cells is essential for understanding their function. The recently introduced fluorescence nanoscopy method called MINSTED has successfully tracked single fluorophore-labelled proteins, albeit in fixed cells and two dimensions only. Here we introduce a MINSTED setup for live-cell tracking of individual proteins in three dimensions (3D) with a localization precision σ down to <1 nm. Applied to the motor protein kinesin-1, our MINSTED nanoscope follows single proteins in 3D as they process along microtubules in 16 nm steps. Individual steps are resolved amid substantial intracellular background. The unique capability of the 3D stimulated emission depletion (STED) beam to carve out the signal of the protein label of interest enables efficient single-molecule investigations at hitherto unpractically high concentrations of labelled proteins and thus in crowded live-cell environments.

item.title: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
item.dc:creator: Yefan Wang
Peter Nienow
Jaime Otero
Daniel N. Goldberg
item.description:
Authors: Yefan Wang, Peter Nienow, Jaime Otero, Daniel N. Goldberg
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a −1 to ~1000 m a −1 before dropping to ~50 m a −1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s −1 ), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

item.title: Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
item.dc:creator: Lea Nussbaum
Emily Zhi Qing Ng
Karmella Naidoo
Janina Nahler
Rosana Ottakandathil Babu
Kyla Dooley
Jessica Soo Weei Ng
Rachel Etherington
item.description:
Authors: Lea Nussbaum, Emily Zhi Qing Ng, Karmella Naidoo, Janina Nahler, Rosana Ottakandathil Babu, Kyla Dooley, Jessica Soo Weei Ng, Rachel Etherington, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to skin homeostasis, but the antigenic targets remain unclear. Whilst CD1a is known to present lipid antigens to effector T cells, the possibility of CD1a presentation to Treg cells us not fully understood. Here, we show CD1a reactivity in subsets of human circulating and cutaneous CD4 + Treg cells, displaying αβ T cell receptors (TCRs), memory phenotypes and suppressive functions, including the ability to secrete interleukin-10 (IL-10) in response to the permissive lipid antigen lysophosphatidylcholine, known to be enriched in skin inflammation. Moreover, CD1a-reactive IL-10-producing CD4 + Treg cells from patients with psoriasis up-regulate type 1 and type 17 pro-inflammatory signatures under in vitro stimulation, while a corresponding Treg cell population is enriched and dysfunctional in psoriatic lesions. Spatial transcriptomic analyses suggest that CD1a-reactive Treg cell signatures are localized in close proximity to CD1a⁺ antigen-presenting cells within psoriatic lesions and are potentially connected through ligand-receptor interactions relevant to cell-cell contact, recruitment, and functional regulation. Furthermore, clonally expanded IL-10-producing Treg cells retain their suppressive phenotype in a CD1a-dependent and TCR-dependent manner. Together, these findings show that subsets of Treg cells are directed to self-lipid antigens and CD1a, but show an altered phenotype equipped with pro-inflammatory potential in the setting of psoriasis.

item.title: Single-molecule landscape of DNA replication pausing
item.dc:creator: Sathish Thiyagarajan
Anna M. Rogers
Carolin A. Müller
Conrad A. Nieduszynski
item.description:
Authors: Sathish Thiyagarajan, Anna M. Rogers, Carolin A. Müller, Conrad A. Nieduszynski
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11569
Abstract: Abstract A pause in DNA synthesis that occurs when the replisome encounters an obstacle could lead to genome instability. Although important, systematic identification of replication pause sites is challenging due to their low frequency and delocalised nature. Here we present a single-molecule identification of sites of replisome perturbation across a eukaryotic genome using long-read nanopore sequencing. For each single-molecule replication pause we determine the direction of replication, leading/lagging-strand identity, location and approximate duration, and whether the replisome resumed synthesis. Although pauses are largely diffuse over the genome, they are significantly enriched over transcribed features and correlate with transcription and R-loop levels. Transcription-replication conflicts are more numerous when head-on than co-directional. Finally, we identify genomic loci with a strong bias towards leading over lagging strand pauses, consistent with uncoupling of the helicase from polymerase epsilon. As one such locus overlaps with an epigenetically-regulated gene, we suggest that helicase-polymerase uncoupling resulting from replication pausing could trigger epigenetic switching.

item.title: Autosomal dosage compensation in aneuploidy and cancer involves transcriptional burst regulation
item.dc:creator: Natali Papanicolaou
Sebastian Wettersten
Guilherme Maia
Antonio Lentini
Björn Reinius
item.description:
Authors: Natali Papanicolaou, Sebastian Wettersten, Guilherme Maia, Antonio Lentini, Björn Reinius
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Aneuploidy, resulting from whole-chromosome or segmental gains and losses, is generally detrimental to organismal fitness and is strongly associated with tumorigenesis. While sex chromosome aneuploidies are relatively well tolerated due to dedicated allelic dosage compensation mechanisms, the existence of comparable regulatory processes for autosomes remains debated. Here, we investigate transcriptional responses to autosomal aneuploidy and identify widespread dosage compensation across affected chromosomes. Using high-sensitivity allele-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing of monoclonal cell expansions spanning diverse ploidies and degrees of aneuploidy, we uncover consistent transcriptional compensation of both chromosomal gains and losses. This response operates in a region-specific manner across both complete and segmental aneuploidies, revealing an unexpected flexibility in dosage regulation. We show that chromosome losses are compensated through increased transcriptional burst frequency from the remaining allele. Complementary proteomics analyses demonstrate additional buffering at the protein level, resulting in a substantial, though still incomplete, restoration of stoichiometric balance across autosomal aneuploid chromosomes for both copy number gains and losses. Analyses of cancer transcriptomes confirm that compensatory mechanisms are active in human tumours. Together, our findings establish dosage compensation as a genome-wide and dynamic response to gene dose imbalance. This mechanism extends beyond sex chromosomes, supports transcriptional homeostasis, and represents a fundamental and evolutionarily conserved mode of gene regulation active across species and in aneuploid cancer cells.

item.title: A macrocyclic peptide inhibitor of the antibiotic transporter NorA
item.dc:creator: Tiffany Suwatthee
Alex Nazzaro
Rupali Singh
Andrew I. Perault
Somrita Dey
Magdalena Podkowik
Priyanka Mishra
Kathryn Tao
item.description:
Authors: Tiffany Suwatthee, Alex Nazzaro, Rupali Singh, Andrew I. Perault, Somrita Dey, Magdalena Podkowik, Priyanka Mishra, Kathryn Tao, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus is a human bacterial pathogen with an array of molecular mechanisms to evade the action of antibiotics. Within the organism, efflux pumps provide a first-line defense mechanism, enabling broad multidrug resistance across antibiotic classes and the ability for the organism to evolve target-level resistance mechanisms. NorA is a key efflux transporter in S. aureus responsible for conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones, puromycin, and other cytotoxic compounds. Here, we describe an approach to develop peptide efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) of NorA by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement and S. aureus growth inhibition. Our cryo-EM structure reveals that a lead peptide NPI-5 inserts deeply into NorA’s substrate binding pocket by using two tryptophan-arginine motifs to bind an anionic patch within NorA, thereby stabilizing the outward-facing conformation of the transporter and halting antibiotic efflux. Further optimization of NPI-5 involving unnatural residues and macrocyclization yielded cNPI-7, a peptide which potentiates fluoroquinolones in vitro and in a murine bacteremia infection model. The successful development of potent and selective peptide-based EPIs provides an approach for inhibiting other efflux systems from pathogenic organisms.

item.title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation in endometriosis
item.dc:creator: Bastien Ducreux
Linda C. Giudice
Marina Sirota
Sally Mortlock
Krina Zondervan
Nilufer Rahmioglu
Merli Saare
Serdar E. Bulun
item.description:
Authors: Bastien Ducreux, Linda C. Giudice, Marina Sirota, Sally Mortlock, Krina Zondervan, Nilufer Rahmioglu, Merli Saare, Serdar E. Bulun, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting 10% of women, characterized by the growth of endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus. Through a genome-wide DNA methylation meta-analysis of nine independent cohorts ( n = 1138 samples), we show an epigenetic dichotomy: the eutopic endometrium of endometriosis cases shows no significant divergence from healthy controls, whereas ectopic lesions exhibit massive, consistent hyper/hypomethylation. We identify 1824 differentially methylated regions targeting the HOX clusters, ESR1 , and GATA2 , key regulators of cell differentiation and hormonal response. This suggests that endometriotic cells possess an epigenetic identity distinct from normal endometrial cells. While most alterations reflect biological mechanisms shared across anatomical sites, distinct signatures exist between lesion types. By harmonizing independent datasets, our study provides a high-resolution molecular map of lesions and strengthens the evidence that DNA methylation drives endometriosis biology.

item.title: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
item.dc:creator: Mengyang Zhou
Mary-Louise Timmermans
Elizabeth Yankovsky
Michael D. Tyka
Matthew C. Long
item.description:
Authors: Mengyang Zhou, Mary-Louise Timmermans, Elizabeth Yankovsky, Michael D. Tyka, Matthew C. Long
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11411
Abstract: Abstract Ocean-based geochemical CO 2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO 2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO 2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

item.title: Intramolecular electrophilic aminations of indoles enable divergent bond migrations to access piperidinoindolines and δ-carbolines
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyan Li
Amu Wang
Peng Liang
Yinxiang Jian
John F. Bower
Xiaofeng Ma
item.description:
Authors: Xiaoyan Li, Amu Wang, Peng Liang, Yinxiang Jian, John F. Bower, Xiaofeng Ma
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract In contrast to well-established C–C migration rearrangements of spiro[indole-3,3’-pyrrolidine] systems, analogous transformations involving isomeric spiro[indole-3,2’-pyrrolidine] frameworks remain unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that unprotected spiro[indole-3,2’-pyrrolidine] intermediates can be generated via acid-catalyzed deprotection of indoles equipped with C3-tethered activated hydroxylamine units. Subsequent migration of the N -center from the C3 to the C2 position of the indolenine is followed by aerobic oxidation or trapping with electrophiles to yield piperidinoindolines. Notably, spiro[indole-3,2’-pyrrolidine] systems with an aryl substituent at C3’ undergo C–C migration in preference to C–N migration, leading to δ-carbolines. Related reactions employing indoles with C2-tethered aminating units are also presented. These strategies offer efficient and concise routes to synthetically challenging piperidinoindoline and δ-carboline scaffolds. The mechanisms of these new processes have been investigated experimentally and via density functional theory calculations. Furthermore, preliminary biological evaluation has revealed potent antitumor activity in selected derivatives.

item.title: ALKR1275Q expands Schwann cell precursor-like cells during sympathoadrenal commitment, creating a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation
item.dc:creator: Mingzhi Liu
Panagiotis Alkinoos Polychronopoulos
Yiming Xia
Ann-Sophie Oppelt
Ana Marin Navarro

item.description:
Authors: Mingzhi Liu, Panagiotis Alkinoos Polychronopoulos, Yiming Xia, Ann-Sophie Oppelt, Ana Marin Navarro, Tzu-Po Chuang, Veronica Zubillaga, Huaitao Cheng, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11914
Abstract: Abstract Neuroblastoma (NB) arises from neural crest-derived cells of the sympathoadrenal lineage, yet how predisposing genetic lesions influence early human development remains poorly understood. Here, we use patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models carrying the familial ALK R1275Q mutation to investigate its role during sympathoadrenal differentiation. We show that ALK R1275Q delays lineage maturation and sustains a proliferative progenitor state characterized by elevated ALK signaling and expansion of a Schwann cell precursor (SCP)-like population. This SCP-like state persists during differentiation and is reduced by ALK inhibition or CRISPR-based mutation correction. Although ALK R1275Q alone is insufficient to drive tumor formation in vivo, it enhances susceptibility to oncogenic transformation in cooperation with MYCN. Together, these findings support a model in which ALK R1275Q reshapes developmental trajectories by maintaining a proliferative SCP-like progenitor state, thereby creating a permissive cellular context for NB initiation.

item.description:
Authors: Júlio Belo Fernandes, Diana Vareta, Sónia Fernandes, Cidália Castro, José João Mendes, João Botelho, Vanessa Machado, Alexandre Trindade, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Climate change, emerging infectious diseases and widening inequalities show that the health of people, animals and ecosystems cannot be separated. However, the ideas we use to understand this interdependence and those we use to organise and practise care have largely developed apart. Here we bring together One Health, linking human, animal and environmental health, and person-centred practice, focused on dignity, relationships and meaningful care. We show where they meet, where they clash and what each offers the other, arguing that care without responsibility for animals and ecosystems is incomplete, as is One Health without attention to lived experience.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Detecting active phage–bacteria interactions in natural microbial communities remains a major limitation for understanding their ecological dynamics and associated co-evolutionary processes. Here, we apply metaHi-C, a chromosome conformation capture method, to resolve active virus–host associations in a freshwater microbial community. From >900 microbial and >33,000 viral Hi-C–assembled genomes, we identify 100 high-confidence phage–host linkages spanning major freshwater bacterial lineages, including Limnohabitans , Acidimicrobium , Synechococcus , Candidatus Nanopelagicus, Candidatus Planktophila, Candidatus Methylopumilus, and Polynucleobacter . The inferred networks reveal signatures consistent with diverse infection patterns, including broad-host-range phages, cellular-level co-infection, kill-the-winner-like dynamics, and one-to-one interactions. These ecological patterns are associated with signatures of diversifying selection in host-interaction genes, consistent with host-range expansion, alongside conserved genomic regions in broad-host-range and co-infecting phages, indicating functional constraints on essential infection modules. Together, these results demonstrate that metaHi-C enables the direct detection of active phage–host associations within a community snapshot, and that, when combined with longitudinal metagenomic recruitment analyses, this approach can link community-level infection dynamics to underlying evolutionary processes, revealing how these forces shape population dynamics of freshwater bacteria.

Abstract: Abstract Modern dietary patterns, particularly those low in fermentable fiber, are associated with intestinal dysbiosis and increased susceptibility to allergic disease, yet individuals exposed to similar diets often display markedly different outcomes. Abstract: Abstract Chemical substitution is an effective strategy to enhance the desired performances of materials based on known structural prototypes. However, it almost invariably introduces intrinsic defects, such as vacancies and twinning defects, which couple with dopants and obscure or degrade the intrinsic properties. Here, we propose a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to overcome this detrimental coupling and successfully apply it to the langasite-family nonlinear optical (NLO) crystal, La 3 TiGa 5 O 14 (LGTi). Overall, this work provides a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to mitigate substitution-induced defects in structurally complex crystalline systems and has great prospects in enhancing material performance.

Abstract: Abstract We experience our limbs as our own, but how does the brain generate this fundamental sense of body ownership? Abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of global efforts to address climate change and promote carbon neutrality, parks, as Nature-based solutions, are often underestimated in their collective carbon sequestration function. Abstract: Abstract Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. Abstract: Abstract Stature is a key indicator of pediatric health, yet the molecular and metabolic architecture governing childhood growth remains incompletely defined. Abstract: Abstract Late spring frost is an intensifying climatic disturbance, yet how frost damage to different organs (leaves and flowers) reshapes reproductive phenology and generates carry-over effects remains unclear. These findings reveal organ-specific pathways through which frost damage reshapes reproductive phenology while generating limited carry-over effects, refining current understanding of phenological responses under climate change.

Such pronounced structural distortions endow TANBC + with unique electronic properties, including a highly positive electrostatic charge on the warped carbon, weak aromaticity, and a low ring bond dissociation energy. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC + participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC + exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. GHG responses varied with pre-conversion wetland type, destination land use, hydrology, and soil carbon and nitrogen status. Our results indicate that GHG responses to coastal wetland conversion are ecosystem- and pathway-specific, underscoring the importance of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

item.description:
Authors: Songze Huo, Xiao-Ming Cao
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

item.description:
Authors: Yueyun Chen, Xin Yi Ling, Jared J. Lodico, Tristan P. O’Neill, B. C. Regan, Matthew Mecklenburg
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract As electronic devices are engineered at increasingly smaller length scales, new nanoscopic metrologies are needed. Measuring nanoscale temperatures and pressures is challenging as physical contact inevitably perturbs the system, and collecting far-field thermal radiation limits the spatial resolution. Kikuchi diffraction thermometry (KDTh), a non-contact scanning electron microscope (SEM) technique, can sensitively map nanoscale temperatures. Local lattice changes measured by Kikuchi pattern fitting enable translating volumetric strain to temperature via the material’s coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE). Measurements on Joule-heated graphite come from rastering a 5.5-nm electron probe across the sample, achieving a ~ 0.01% fractional precision and 2.2 K/ $$\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}$$ Hz temperature sensitivity. KDTh offers superior sensitivity by fitting the entire Kikuchi pattern, instead of a particular Kikuchi band or interband angle. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) techniques can achieve a similar precision, but electron-transparency limits their applications. KDTh can operate in both transmission and reflection modes to cost-effectively accommodate a variety of samples.

Abstract: Abstract Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound cannot be reconstituted in a heterologous host, suggesting that one or more enzymes required for biosynthesis are missing. The missing enzymes includes a pathogenesis-related (PR)10 family protein that likely catalyzes cyclization of a transient intermediate. Careful analysis of gene expression profiles in leaf and root also enabled the discovery of four additional enzymes that convert an upstream intermediate to ibophyllidine. This work reveals the chemical logic that generates two distinct alkaloid scaffolds in this important medicinal plant.

Abstract: Abstract Solar-blind Ga 2 O 3 -based photodetectors, sensing deep ultraviolet (DUV) light (200–280 nm), offer unparalleled opportunities for secure non-line-of-sight optical communication. This work not only resolves the longstanding gain-bandwidth trade-off in DUV photodetection but also presents a universal band-engineering framework for next-generation optoelectronics.

Abstract: Abstract Influenza A virus causes acute damage to airway epithelium, yet the damage–repair cycle and mechanisms underlying persistent mucociliary clearance (MCC) dysfunction long after viral clearance remain unclear. Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence promises democratized access to dermatological care, but model reliability depends on the quality and comprehensiveness of the underlying data. Abstract: Abstract Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Early studies characterized nidovirus DMVs as sealed compartments, leaving it unclear how newly synthesized viral RNA could be exported to the cytosol. Despite the substantial evolutionary distance separating arteriviruses and coronaviruses, we observe DMV-spanning pore complexes with striking structural similarities to those previously described in coronaviruses. These pores may facilitate both export and encapsidation of viral RNA. In the absence of viral RNA synthesis, ectopic expression of the arterivirus transmembrane nonstructural proteins nsp2 and nsp3 suffices to induce the formation of pore-containing DMVs. Together, our findings reveal the conservation of key structural features of DMV pores across two distantly related nidovirus families and support a central role for these pores in nidovirus replication.

Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11877
Abstract: Abstract Given the large size of neurons, local maintenance of mitochondria is crucial to counteract insults to this organelle in axons and dendrites. The Parkinson-related mitochondrial kinase PINK1 plays a central role in mitochondrial quality control, which in neurons requires the transport of Pink1 mRNA by mitochondrial hitch-hiking. However, how and where PINK1 is locally translated and processed has remained unclear. Using live-cell imaging, we trace local PINK1 translation sites and preprotein dynamics, revealing a concerted interplay between mitochondria and the ER, with endolysosomes frequently localized adjacent to the site of translation. Upon metabolically regulated untethering from mitochondria, Pink1 mRNA relocates to ribosomes in proximity to the ER and endolysosomes for translation of the PINK1 preprotein. The ER chaperone DNAJB6 shields the PINK1 preprotein in transit to mitochondria, following the post-translational ER-SURF pathway. Consequently, loss of DNAJB6 leads to persistent ER/endolysosome-associated PINK1 precursor stores and failure of mitophagy upon mitochondrial damage. Our findings reveal that neuronal PINK1 protein translation switches between mitochondrially anchored co-translational and ER-associated post-translational import states, with functional implications for mitochondrial quality control.

item.title: A spectral framework for revealing the hidden low-dimensional structure in stochastic reaction networks
item.dc:creator: Ankit Gupta
Mustafa Khammash
item.description:
Authors: Ankit Gupta, Mustafa Khammash
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Stochastic reaction networks govern noise-driven dynamics in systems ranging from gene regulation to cellular signalling and population processes. Yet their high dimensionality and sensitivity to initial states obscure transient mechanisms and limit reliable inference from experimental data. Here, we show that stochastic reaction networks in biological systems often exhibit dominant low-dimensional spectral structure that shapes their dynamics. We develop a spectral framework based on the stochastic Koopman operator that identifies these dominant dynamical modes directly from simulated trajectories, yielding reduced representations with computable error bounds. This reduction enables accurate analytical descriptions of the time evolution of moments, parameter sensitivities, and cross-spectral densities, while achieving order-of-magnitude computational gains relative to standard simulation-based methods. Applied to synthetic gene circuits, our framework reveals the spectral organisation of stochastic oscillators, enables systematic comparison of competing intracellular controllers, and facilitates inference of initial-state distributions from single-cell snapshot population data collected over time. Together, these results establish a principled spectral description of stochastic reaction dynamics and provide a foundation for analysing and inferring high-dimensional noise-driven biological systems.

Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11875
Abstract: Abstract Anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) has been proposed as a source of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) at marine cold seeps, but the underlying molecular mechanism for its production remains unknown. Here we demonstrate a previously unrecognized link between AOM and porewater DOC by analyzing disaccharides in sediment and porewaters from a methane-charged cold seep in Astoria Canyon (Oregon, USA). In the AOM zone, sediments contain up to 17.7 mg L −1 trehalose with δ 13 C values as low as −78‰, and porewaters contain up to 1 mg L −1 sucrose with δ 13 C values as low as −66‰, representing 4.6% of DOC. Stable isotope probing experiments reveal AOM-dependent biosynthesis of trehalose and sucrose, and both disaccharides turn over faster than diagnostic lipids, suggesting that these compounds serve as biomarkers for active AOM. Accordingly, disaccharides mediate a relationship that may sustain microbial food webs and influence carbon cycling in methane-rich marine sediments.

Authors: Rubén Soussé Villa, Oriol Jorba, María Gonçalves Ageitos, Jeronimo Escribano, Vincenzo Obiso, Ron L. Miller, Longlei Li, Natalie M. Mahowald, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Mineral dust affects atmospheric chemistry, air quality, and climate, yet its impacts remain uncertain because its mineral composition is poorly constrained. Here we combine NASA EMIT orbital imaging spectroscopy with a satellite-constrained global chemistry model to quantify how source-resolved calcite variability alters aerosol chemistry and optical properties. EMIT-derived calcite improves agreement with airborne observations and reveals contrasts in dust alkalinity. Compared with globally averaged calcite, source-resolved calcite shifts regional annual mean aerosol pH by -0.6 to +0.5 units, with local changes exceeding 1 pH unit across substantial areas of the most affected dust-influenced regions, reaching -4 to +3 units in limited areas. These acidity changes reorganize secondary inorganic aerosol formation, nitrate partitioning, and extreme nitrate events, particularly where dust interacts with anthropogenic pollution. In contrast, calcite-driven secondary-aerosol radiative effects are small relative to those caused by spatial variations in iron-oxide absorption. These results show that calcite variability strongly modulates heterogeneous chemistry, whereas iron oxides dominate radiative impacts.
